name: Auto-CoT (Automatic Chain-of-Thought)
executive_summary: Automatically construct a diverse set of few-shot CoT exemplars by clustering unlabeled questions and generating reasoning chains for one representative per cluster — no manual exemplar writing at all.
description: Clusters a pool of unlabeled questions by similarity, picks one representative question per cluster (favoring simpler, shorter questions to reduce generated-chain error), and generates a Zero-Shot-CoT reasoning chain for each representative automatically. The resulting set is used directly as the few-shot exemplar block, removing both the manual-writing cost of hand-built CoT and the cost of Active Prompting's human-in-the-loop annotation step.
when_to_use: Building a reusable few-shot CoT exemplar set fully automatically, with no human annotation budget at all.
when_not_to_use: A small human-annotation budget is available — Active Prompting's uncertainty-targeted human annotation generally yields higher-quality exemplars.
known_pitfalls: Automatically generated chains for the cluster representatives can themselves be wrong, silently propagating an incorrect reasoning pattern into every prompt that reuses the exemplar set.

primary_source.title: Automatic Chain of Thought Prompting in Large Language Models

usage_templates.template:
# Cluster
Cluster this pool of unlabeled questions into {{num_clusters}} groups by similarity: {{unlabeled_question_pool}}

# Select representative + generate chain (per cluster)
Representative question: {{cluster_representative_question}}
Let's think step by step.
(the resulting chain becomes one exemplar in the final few-shot block)

# Assemble
Concatenate all {{num_clusters}} generated exemplars into a single few-shot CoT prompt prefix for future questions.

variables.name: unlabeled_question_pool
variables.description: Pool of unlabeled candidate questions to cluster

variables.name: num_clusters
variables.description: How many clusters (= how many few-shot exemplars) to produce

variables.name: cluster_representative_question
variables.description: The chosen representative question for one cluster

usage_templates.reproducibility_note: A single LLM call (or a fixed sequence of them) with no external system dependency; running this template again at temperature 0 against the same model version should reproduce the same output.
